page.title: Free Stroop Test Online
page.meta_description: A free Stroop test in your browser: name the ink color, not the word. One minute, then your Stroop effect, accuracy and average time.
page.lead: A color word appears in colored ink. Answer with the color of the ink, not the word, as fast as you can. After one minute you get your Stroop effect: how much slower you are when the word and the ink don't match. Nothing to install, nothing sent anywhere.
page.aria_idle: Test area. Press Start, then answer with the ink color.
page.aria_running: Test running. Answer with the ink color using the buttons, or keys 1 to 6.
page.aria_finished: Test finished. Your results are shown below the test area.
page.aria_stopped: Test stopped. Your partial results are shown below the test area.
page.question: What color is the ink?
page.keys_hint: On a keyboard, keys 1 to 6 answer in the order of the buttons.
page.effect_hint: Above zero: you were slower when the word and the ink differed. That is the usual result.
page.note_final: Difference in average time between mismatched and matching words · {n} answers in {s} s.
page.note_stopped: Stopped before the end · {n} answers. This run is not saved.
page.note_few: Too few correct answers to interpret this difference.
page.history_empty: No test saved in this browser.
page.confirm_clear: Clear the tests saved in this browser?
page.read_p1: Reading is automatic: you read the word before you can stop yourself. When the word names another color than its ink, you have to hold back that first answer, and that takes time. The Stroop effect is that extra time, in milliseconds.
page.read_p2: Most people answer more slowly on mismatched words, often by several tens of milliseconds. Fatigue, distraction and practice all move the result, so compare yourself with yourself, at the same time of day.
page.read_p3: This test measures one kind of attention control on one task. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not a clinical attention test.
page.cta_title: Want three test lengths, in 17 languages?
page.cta_p1: The {link} offers tests of 30 seconds, 1 minute and 3 minutes, explains each number and lets you share a result.
page.cta_p2: It is made by the team behind {upchin}, an iPhone app that helps you cut down on distracting apps with Apple's Screen Time.
page.footer: Open source, a single HTML file, no tracking. Your results stay in your browser's local storage.

readme.title: Free Stroop test online
readme.intro: A free Stroop test that runs in your browser, in a single HTML file.
readme.how: A color word appears in colored ink. Answer with the color of the ink, not the word, with the buttons or the keys 1 to 6. After one minute you get:
readme.def_effect: **Stroop effect**: how much slower you answer when the word and the ink differ than when they match.
readme.def_accuracy: **Correct answers**: the share of right answers.
readme.def_mean: **Average time**: your average answer time, on correct answers only.
readme.def_split: **Word matches ink / differs from ink**: the two averages the Stroop effect is computed from.
readme.method: Each block of trials has as many matching as mismatching words, with every ink color equally often, and never the same word and ink twice in a row. Only correct answers count in the times.
readme.storage: The last ten tests are kept in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent anywhere: no tracking, no external script, no sign-up.
readme.run: Open `index.html` in any browser. No build step and no dependency.
readme.reading_p1: Most people answer more slowly when the word names another color than its ink, often by several tens of milliseconds. Fatigue, distraction and practice all move the result, so compare yourself with yourself, at the same time of day.
readme.reading_p2: This test measures one kind of attention control on one task. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not a clinical attention test.
